literature_proposed.summary: No proof is known. The statement says that the distance from N!·S to the nearest integer does not tend to 0, where S = sum_{n>=2} 1/(n!-1); equivalently, in the factorial number system S = sum a_n/n! with 0 <= a_n <= n-1, it says min(a_n, n-a_n) >= delta·n for some delta > 0 and infinitely many n (up to the shift of index). Its position: it implies erdos-68--h3 (with the proved tail split erdos-68--h2), which implies the irrationality of S; it is not known to follow from either. For comparison, e is the standard number for which N!·e does tend to the integers (N!·e is an integer plus sum_{j>N} N!/j! < 1/N), and S = (e-2) + T with T = sum_{n>=2} 1/(n!(n!-1)), so the statement is equivalent to the same one for T; in particular it implies that T, equivalently S - e, is irrational, which the irrationality of S alone does not give. No result on N!·x modulo 1 for this S or T is known to us.
